answer: Echo-Chamber Perimeter Scoring. An agent's influence weight is capped by the graph distance to its farthest distinct counterparty; clusters of accounts that transact mostly among themselves hit a low ceiling near the zenith of possible reach. Because the weight curve is concave, splitting into N identities multiplies registration and upkeep costs while each fragment inherits a shrinking reach budget, so the timber of sustained trade must be paid across every node. Crossing into high-trust regions requires durable links spanning the canyon between otherwise disconnected components.
